newsitem.title: UK: SuedwestLB reaches out to new Eurobond investors.
newsitem.headline: SuedwestLB reaches out to new Eurobond investors.

text.p: Suedwestdeutsche Landesbank, the triple-A rated German state-owned bank, on Monday completed a year-long strategy of establishing itself with new investors.

A $300 million three-year bond aimed at Japanese retail investors was launched today, hot on the heels of a $750 million five-year benchmark deal issued last week -- its first institutionally-targeted bond.
"I don't envisage anything large-scale taking place (this year)," a SuedwestLB treasury official told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"We might do another transaction if a deal fulfills strategic rather than monetary objectives, but these issues take time to prepare," he said.
"There is a possibility of a mark deal, but I have nothing planned," the official said.
The SuedwestLB treasury team has spent a lot of time on the road in an effort to replicate its strong European retail following among institutions.

"Having developed one of the best retail followings in Europe, we wanted to take the next step and indicate to institutional investors, particularly in the Far East, that they should regard us as an issuer of note," the official said.

"We have the credit quality, we have the size. What we needed to prove (to institutions) was we also have the awareness to provide bonds to the market that they are going to like," the treasury official said.
"Last Friday's issue was a step in the direction. It was a big step, and by all accounts a successful one," he said.
SuedwestLB has borrowed around $3.5 billion in 1996 from both private and public international bond markets. In 1995 the total was $5.3 billion from the public markets alone.
"This year's amount is quite a lot shy of last year's, but we wanted to take a breather to allow people to adjust to our more selective approach," the SuedwestLB official said.
Part of this strategy involved targeting European institutions ahead of increased competition among borrowers if European economic and monetary union (EMU) takes place in 1999.
"We need to look at all core European currencies, where (after EMU) investors will start to invest in a wider range of borrowers in a single currency," the official said.
"We will also become part of a bigger picture on the borrowing side, (competing with) not just Germans but French and Dutch credits too," he said.
SuedwestLB issued a strategic French franc issue last week, and plans to launch deals in marks, guilders and lire, the official said.
